situation:
You are the brand manager at COPPER FURROW DISTILLERY, a craft distillery that makes whiskey and gin in a converted grain mill. Six months ago COPPER FURROW DISTILLERY merged with a smaller distillery down the valley, and the two labels have still not been brought together into one. The president (judge) has asked you to recommend how the merged company should sell what it makes.

The merger was built on the idea of a single premium label carrying one story. The comments visitors leave in the tasting room say something else. They come for the tour and for the story of the mill, and they say the new blended label confuses them on the shelf. The company's file of those comments is the clearest information it holds about how it is positioned.

A national distributor has offered to carry the bottles in nine hundred stores. That partnership would bring the revenue the merged company needs to pay down the debt it took on, but the distributor would set the label design, the price point and which expressions get made, so COPPER FURROW DISTILLERY would give up the story its tasting room visitors say they come for.

Staying independent keeps control of the label and keeps the tasting room, which sells an afternoon and a tour rather than a bottle off a shelf. It also leaves the merged company selling in one small region and paying down the merger debt slowly. Under the merger agreement, the founder of the smaller distillery keeps a say in the label for two more years either way.

The president (judge) wants you to identify what advantage the merged company actually has, to weigh the two courses against each other, and to recommend one of them. The president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and after you have presented and answered questions, the president (judge) will thank you for your time.
judgeCharacterization:

You have asked your brand manager to identify what advantage the merged company actually has, to weigh the national distributor's offer to carry the bottles in nine hundred stores against staying independent with the tasting room, and to recommend one of the two.
